newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA allies to cancel Spain protest if appeal fails.
newsitem.headline: ETA allies to cancel Spain protest if appeal fails.

text.p: The political wing of the Basque guerrilla organisation ETA said on Thursday it had appealed against a government ban on Saturday's demonstration and that it would abide by the judge's decision.
Herri Batasuna, political arm of the ETA separatist group which sparked national outrage by killing a young town councillor last weekend, said a judge was expected to rule on the issue on Friday.

On Wednesday, officials in the Basque region barred ETA supporters from demonstrating in San Sebastian for fear that it would ignite more violence following the rebels' assassination of Miguel Angel Blanco.
"There's no demonstration on Saturday unless the judge says that it is legal," Herri Batasuna leader Floren Aoiz told reporters.
He said that if Herri Batasuna was not allowed to go ahead with the protest, they would ask for permission to demonstrate on July 27.

With Spain still seething with anger against ETA, officials were worried a rally by rebel supporters so soon after Blanco's death would unleash a wave of sectarian clashes that could spread from the Basque region in the north to the rest of the country.
Millions of Spaniards have taken to the streets to express outrage at Blanco's death on Sunday. While most gatherings have been peaceful, there have also been sporadic attacks on ETA sympathisers.
Spanish politicians have branded Herri Batasuna as "accomplices" to murder, but the group claims it is being targeted for a "political lynching."
The radical political party won 14.3 percent of the Basque vote in the 1995 municipal elections and holds two seats in the national congress.
